message.content:
**Order filled:** Bought 44 shares of AAPL at $222.90 (≈$9,808, filled at the limit).

**Summary — what I did and why.** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024‑09‑28, filed 2024‑11‑01), this morning's feed, and the latest news, then checked the live quote ($222.70 last, bid/ask $222.68/$222.72) and the account (no AAPL position, $50,000 cash, no other orders today). The fundamentals support a small, single buy within mandate: total net sales of **$391,035M**, net income of **$93,736M** and diluted EPS of **$6.08** — the earnings figure depressed by a disclosed one-time $10.2bn State Aid tax charge — with operating income of $123,216M and very strong operating cash flow of **$118,254M**, gross margin up to 46.2%, Services growing 13% to $96,169M, and $140.8bn of unrestricted cash/securities against a still-rising buyback ($95.0bn repurchased in FY24, new $110bn authorization). Offsets I weighed: revenue growth of only 2% (iPhone roughly flat, Greater China −8%), a 24.1% effective tax rate, and the ongoing DOJ/EU DMA antitrust and App Store overhangs — none of which changes the thesis. The tape was uneventful (shares "little changed" around $222, the feed's early prints drifting from ~$221.8 to ~$220.5, offset by mildly constructive iPhone 16 supplier-build headlines and unchanged holiday-quarter analyst estimates), so rather than chase or wait, I placed one aggressive-but-near-market limit buy: 44 shares at $222.90 (~0.1% above the last trade), roughly $9,808, comfortably under the $10,000 per-order cap and the $20,000 daily cap, buy-only, with no money moved out of the account (remaining cash ≈ $40,190 and the existing 100 MSFT shares untouched). Had the stock not cooperated, I would have simply let the order lapse rather than raise the price.
